disclaimer: PortDoctor is a static, text-level scanner. Nothing here was compiled or run against a QNX SDP. Rules marked 'guess' are unverified claims about QNX 8.0 and must be checked against the SDP.

findings.title: Raw Linux syscall()
findings.message: Linux syscall numbers (SYS_*, __NR_*) have no meaning on QNX (known: QNX is not a Linux kernel).
findings.remedy: Replace each call with the libc/POSIX function it wraps, but check the semantics: pthread_self() is NOT a replacement for gettid (it returns an opaque pthread_t, not a numeric kernel thread id): decide what the id is for (logging, per-thread keys) and use pthread_self() only where an opaque handle is enough; a numeric thread id may need a QNX-specific call (check the SDP; guess). futex has no mechanical replacement: it is a redesign onto pthread mutex/condvar.
findings.verify: verify against SDP: whether gettid() or another numeric thread-id call exists.

context.text: /* Might help on systems with wireless */
/* Mostly network visible but useful in some situations.

findings.message: QNX has a /proc, but it is a different interface (process address spaces, not Linux text files).
findings.remedy: Replace with POSIX/QNX queries: sysconf(), getrusage(), the system page (<sys/syspage.h>) for CPU/memory facts, procfs ioctls (DCMD_PROC_*) for process info.
findings.verify: verify against SDP: procfs layout on QNX 8.0.

findings.title: Includes a Linux-specific <sys/...> header
findings.message: This glibc/Linux <sys/...> header is believed to be absent from the QNX 8.0 SDP.
findings.remedy: Remove the include together with the calls it supports (see the per-API findings), or guard it with #if defined(__linux__) and add a __QNXNTO__ branch.
findings.verify: verify against SDP: grep $QNX_TARGET/usr/include for the header.

findings.title: Includes a Linux kernel header
findings.message: <linux/...> and <asm/...> are Linux kernel uapi headers. The QNX SDP is not believed to ship them (guess; not checked against an SDP). Many uses are trivial (linux/limits.h, linux/types.h can often be replaced by POSIX headers); device-ioctl headers are not.
findings.remedy: Replace each use with the POSIX/QNX equivalent of what the header supplied (types, constants). If it is a device ioctl header, the device needs a QNX resource-manager interface instead.
findings.verify: verify against SDP: ls $QNX_TARGET/usr/include/linux and asm* before treating these as missing.

findings.title: Makefile branches on uname

findings.remedy: Key the logic on a target variable (for example TARGET_OS passed on the command line) rather than uname of the build machine.

findings.title: Linux-specific socket options

context.text: TRACE(("set_listen_fast_open failed for socket %d: %s", sock, strerror(errno)))

findings.message: Socket options that originated on Linux. Some exist on BSD-derived stacks with a different meaning or struct layout (TCP_FASTOPEN and TCP_INFO exist on FreeBSD; TCP_INFO's struct differs). QNX 8.0 networking (io-sock) is BSD-derived (guess), so BSD-style APIs may be present, so presence on 8.0 must be checked per option (guess). Not all of these are Linux-only.
findings.remedy: Guard each setsockopt/getsockopt with #ifdef so it compiles away when the macro is undefined. If the macro IS defined, confirm the semantics and struct layout before relying on a same-named constant (TCP_INFO in particular).
findings.verify: verify against SDP: grep each option in $QNX_TARGET/usr/include/netinet/tcp.h and sys/socket.h.
